rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayd takes qurʾ as a transition from one state to another.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : وهو قول أبي عبيد : أنه عبارة عن الانتقال من حالة إلى حالة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ says qurʾ means a time or appointed period, such as the time when stars rise or set or winds blow; Hudhalī poetry witnesses this usage.
rows.anchor: والقول الثالث : وهو قول أبي عمرو بن العلاء : أن القرء هو الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If qurʾ means an appointed time, it can include either menstruation or purity, since each has its own defined time.
rows.anchor: وإذا ثبت أن القرء هو الوقت دخل فيه الحيض والطهر ، لأن لكل واحد منهما وقتا معينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse's surface could suggest any three units called qurūʾ, scholars agree a woman must count three of the same kind; they disagree whether these are purity periods or menstruations.
rows.anchor: والظاهر يقتضي أنها إذا اعتدت بثلاثة أشياء تسمى ثلاثة أقراء أن تخرج عن عهدة التكليف ، إلا أن العلماء أجمعوا على أنه لا يكفي ذلك

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī counts the three qurūʾ as periods of purity; Rāzī reports this also from Ibn ʿUmar, Zayd, ʿĀʾisha, the seven jurists, Mālik, Rabīʿa, and Aḥmad in one narration.
rows.anchor: فمذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنها الأطهار ، روى ذلك عن ابن عمر ، وزيد ، وعائشة

rows.speaker: علي وعمر وابن مسعود
rows.claim: ʿAlī, ʿUmar, and Ibn Masʿūd count the qurūʾ as menstruations; Abū Ḥanīfa, al-Thawrī, al-Awzāʿī, Ibn Abī Laylā, Ibn Shubruma, and Isḥāq share this position.
rows.anchor: وقال علي وعمر وابن مسعود هي الحيض ، وهو قول أبي حنيفة ، والثوري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Counting purity makes the waiting period shorter: the remainder of purity after divorce counts and it ends when the third menstruation begins. In the Ḥanafī account, it ends only after the third menstruation if divorce was during purity, or the fourth if during menstruation; after maximum menstruation it ends before bathing, but after minimum menstruation only with bathing, dry ablution if water is absent, or the passing of a prayer time.
rows.anchor: فائدة الخلاف أن مدة العدة عند الشافعي أقصر ، وعندهم أطول

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues from 65:1 that divorce is for the time when the waiting period begins; since divorce during menstruation is forbidden, the waiting period begins in purity.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { النساء فطلقوهن لعدتهن } ( الطلاق : 1 ) ومعناه في وقت عدتهن

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The author of al-Kashshāf explains 65:1 as meaning divorce them with their waiting period still in the future, as in saying there are three days left in a month.
rows.anchor: أجاب صاحب ( الكشاف ) عنه فقال بمعنى مستقبلات لعدتهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the al-Kashshāf gloss strengthens al-Shāfiʿī: divorce can occur throughout purity, so the purity period beginning after divorce must count toward the waiting period.
rows.anchor: وأقول هذا الكلام يقوى استدلال الشافعي رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha says that the qurūʾ are periods of purity.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها قالت : هل تدرون الأقراء ؟ الأقراء الأطهار

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī adds that women know this matter best because they experience it.
rows.anchor: ثم قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : والنساء بهذا أعلم ، لأن هذا إنما يبتلي به النساء

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: The gathering sense of qurʾ is supported by usage: a camel that has not gathered offspring, the womb gathering menstrual blood, a basin gathering water, stars gathering before setting, and the Qurʾān gathering letters, words, and sciences; ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm's verse is also cited.
rows.anchor: يقال : ما قرأت الناقة نسلا قط ، أي ما جمعت في رحمها ولدا قط ومنه قول عمرو بن كلثوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a further argument for purity, Rāzī says menstrual blood does not collect in the womb but flows drop by drop; during purity it gathers in the body and accumulates toward its fullest state at the end, making the end of purity the complete qurʾ.
rows.anchor: قلنا : الدماء لا تجتمع في الرحم ألبتة بل تنفصل قطرة قطرة أما وقت الطهر فالكل مجتمع في البدن

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues that no one should have power to detain another person's freedom without proof; therefore the shorter count of three purity periods is required, not the extra time added by counting menstruations.
rows.anchor: أن الأصل أن لا يكون لأحد على أحد من العقلاء المكلفين حق الحبس والمنع من التصرفات

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues that either purity or menstruation can be called qurʾ, but purity is the shorter count; a woman may not be required to wait through the excess time, so menstruation is not obligatory.
rows.anchor: وكل واحد من الطهر ومن الحيض يسمى بهذا الاسم ، فوجب أن تخرج المرأة عن العهدة بأيهما كان

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa argues that although qurūʾ can lexically mean purity or menstruation, legal usage favors menstruation, citing the Prophet's instruction to stop praying during one's qurūʾ.
rows.anchor: لما روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( دعي الصلاة أيام أقرائك )

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The Ḥanafī argument says menstruation better fits three complete qurūʾ: counting purity can end the waiting period after only two full purities and part of a third.
rows.anchor: أن القول بأن الأقراء حيض يمكن معه استيفاء ثلاثة أقراء بكمالها

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī answers by analogy with the hajj months in 2:197, a plural counted as three although the hajj period includes only part of the third month.
rows.anchor: أجاب الشافعي رضي الله عنه عن ذلك أن الله قال : { الحج أشهر معلومات } ( الحج : 197 )

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilī al-Jubbāʾī rejects the analogy: the apparent count in 2:197 was left for evidence, while no such evidence permits leaving the apparent three here; unlike hajj months, the waiting period is continuous and must be completed.
rows.anchor: أجاب الجبائي من شيوخ المعتزلة عن هذا الجواب من وجهين الأول : أنا تركنا الظاهر في تلك الآية لدليل

rows.speaker: المتأخرون من أصحابنا
rows.claim: Rāzī's later colleagues answer that counting menstruations also creates a partial unit when divorce occurs during purity, but that excess is necessary because divorce during menstruation is forbidden; under the purity reading, the purity in which divorce occurs counts.
rows.anchor: وإجاب المتأخرون من أصحابنا عن هذه الحجة من وجهين الأول : كما أن حمل الأقراء على الأطهار يوجب النقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī replies that if qurʾ means gathering, the full gathering is reached at the end of purity, so counting purity does not make any qurʾ incomplete.
rows.anchor: بينا أن القرء اسم للاجتماع وكمال الاجتماع إنما يحصل في آخر الطهر قرءا تاما

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The Ḥanafī side argues from 65:4: months replace menstruations for women without menses, and a substitute is counted in complete units; therefore the replaced qurūʾ must also be complete menstruations, not two purities and part of a third.
rows.anchor: فقال : { واللائى يئسن من المحيض من نسائكم إن ارتبتم فعدتهن ثلاثة أشهر } ( الطلاق : 4 )

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says an enslaved woman's divorce is two divorces and her waiting period is two menstruations; since her waiting period is half that of a free woman, the argument infers that a free woman's qurūʾ are menstruations.
rows.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( طلاق الأمة تطليقتان ، وعدتها حيضتان )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ḥanafī argument cites consensus that a purchased enslaved woman is cleared for intercourse by one menstruation, then equates the purpose of that waiting with divorce iddah.
rows.anchor: أجمعنا على أن الاستبراء في شراء الجواري يكون بالحيضة ، فكذا العدة تكون بالحيضة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The Ḥanafī argument says the main purpose of iddah is to establish that the womb is clear, which menstruation establishes and purity does not.
rows.anchor: أن الغرض الأصلي في العدة استبراء الرحم ، والحيض هو الذي تستبرأ به الأرحام دون الطهر

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The Ḥanafī position is presented as precaution: at the point when a new marriage would be permitted under the purity view, the menstruation view still forbids it; the argument gives priority to prohibition, the presumption that sexual relations are forbidden, and avoiding doubt.
rows.anchor: أن القول بأل القروء هي الحيض احتياط وتغليب لجانب الحرمة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The argument cites the Prophet's maxim that when lawful and forbidden considerations meet, the forbidden prevails, and his instruction to leave what causes doubt for what does not.
rows.anchor: لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( ما اجتمع الحرام والحلال إلا وغلب الحرام الحلال )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī concludes that the competing proofs weaken preference; for each person, God's ruling is what their own ijtihād leads them to.
rows.anchor: عند تعارض هذه الوجوه تضعف الترجيحات ، ويكون حكم الله في حق الكل ما أدى اجتهاده إليه

words: وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the end of iddah depends on menstruation or childbirth, facts men cannot directly know, the woman is trusted to report her status and her claim of ending iddah is accepted when the elapsed time permits it.
rows.anchor: جعلت المرأة أمينة في العدة ، وجعل القول قولها إذا ادعت انقضاء قرئها في مدة يمكن ذلك فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On al-Shāfiʿī's calculation, the shortest possible iddah is thirty-two days and one hour: a purity at divorce, a minimum one-day-and-night menses, fifteen days of purity, another minimum menses, fifteen days of purity, then renewed bleeding.
rows.anchor: وهو على مذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه اثنان وثلاثون يوما وساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pregnant woman who claims that she miscarried is likewise believed because she is treated as trustworthy in this matter.
rows.anchor: وكذلك إذا كانت حاملا فادعت أنها أسقطت كان القول قولها

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: One interpretation includes both pregnancy and menstruation: a woman might conceal pregnancy to shorten iddah, avoid the first husband's return, marry another, or have a child attributed to the later husband.
rows.anchor: الأول : أنه الحبل والحيض معا ، وذلك لأن المرأة لها أغراض كثيرة في كتمانهما

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Under the same interpretation, a woman might conceal menstruation to lengthen iddah so her first husband returns, or shorten it to defeat his right of return, by hiding an early, third, or ongoing menses.
rows.anchor: وأما كتمان الحيض فغرضها فيه أن المرأة إذا طلقها الزوج وهي من ذوات الأقراء فقد تحب تطويل عدتها

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: A second interpretation restricts the concealed matter to pregnancy: it cites 3:6, says menstruation is outside rather than created in the womb, and considers a child nobler than menstrual blood; Rāzī rejects these reasons and includes all such hidden states because they change marriage's lawful status.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني : أن المراد هو النهي عن كتمان الحمل فقط ، واحتجوا عليه بوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects restricting the phrase to pregnancy: its purpose is to forbid hiding private conditions that others cannot know and that alter whether marriage is lawful, so it covers them all.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذه الوجوه ضعيفة ، لأنه لما كان المقصود منعها عن إخفاء هذه الأحوال

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: A third interpretation restricts the warning to menstruation because it follows mention of qurūʾ and pregnancy had not yet been mentioned; Rāzī rejects the restriction, reading the clause as independent and inclusive of all that is created in the womb.
rows.anchor: القول الثالث : المراد هو النهي عن كتمان الحيض ، لأن هذه الآية وردت عقيب ذكر الإقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the clause is a self-contained statement rather than a continuation limited by the preceding mention of qurūʾ, and so it covers everything created in the womb.
rows.anchor: لأن قوله : { ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله فى أرحامهن } كلام مستأنف مستقل بنفسه

words: إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faith phrase is not a condition making the prohibition apply only to believers; like telling an oppressor that a believer should not oppress, it is a severe threat to women.
rows.anchor: فليس المراد أن ذلك النهي مشروط بكونها مؤمنة ، بل هذا كما تقول للرجل الذي يظلم

words: إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī links the threat to 2:283: concealing testimony makes the heart sinful, and a person entrusted with something must return the trust and fear God; betraying entrusted responsibility is grave.
rows.anchor: وهو كما قال في الشهادة { ومن يكتمها فإنه ءاثم قلبه } ( البقرة : 283 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis takes buʿūla as a plural of baʿl, like other collective plurals; the feminine ending reinforces the group's feminine form and is permitted only in established Arabic usage, not with every noun.
rows.anchor: أنه جمع بعل ، كالفحولة والذكورة والجدودة والعمومة ، وهذه الهاء زائدة مؤكدة لتأنيث الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿl can name either spouse: a woman may be called baʿla or zawja, while zawj is the more eloquent term; baʿl originally means master or owner, and was also the name of an idol taken as lord.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن اسم البعل مما يشترك فيه الزوجان فيقال للمرأة بعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis takes buʿūla as a verbal noun for becoming a husband; bāʿala can mean intercourse, and usage in reports about the days of tashrīq and good treatment of husbands supports reading the phrase as their husbands.
rows.anchor: أن العبولة مصدر ، يقال : بعل الرجل يبعل بعولة ، إذا صار بعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī explains aḥaqq as the first husband's greater right during iddah: concealment could make a later marriage appear possible, or a woman's claim that iddah ended could give another man an apparent right.
rows.anchor: فإذا فعلن ذلك كان الزوج الأول أحق بردهن ، وذلك لأنه ثبت للزوج الثاني حق في الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that the waiting woman has a right to end the marriage by letting iddah pass, while the husband's revocation can cancel that right, so he is called more entitled to take her back.
rows.anchor: إذا كانت معتدة فلها في مضي العدة حق انقطاع النكاح فلما كان لهن هذا الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Radd means to return or restore; Rāzī cites the wording in 18:36 and a parallel expression using rajʿa.
rows.anchor: يقال : رددته أي رجعته قال تعالى في موضع { ولئن رددت إلى ربى } ( الكهف : 36 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a revocably divorced woman remains a wife during iddah, revocation is called a return because it ends the waiting and monitoring; on al-Shāfiʿī's view it also changes her from forbidden intimacy back to permissibility.
rows.anchor: أن الرد والرجعة يتضمن إبطال التربص والتحري في العدة فهي ما دامت في العدة كأنه كانت جارية

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds that intimacy with a revocably divorced wife is forbidden until the husband formally revokes the divorce.
rows.anchor: ومذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنه يحرم الاستمتاع بها إلا بعد الرجعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī explains rajula through strength and power, with examples of a strong man, a horse able to walk, forceful speech without deliberation, and daylight growing bright; daraja means a rank or step on a road, from the image of life and travel unfolding stage by stage.
rows.anchor: يقال : رجل بين الرجلة ، أي القوة ، وهو أرجل الرجلين أي أقواهما ، وفرس رجيل قوي على المشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of men's degree lists advantages in intellect, blood money, inheritance, leadership and legal roles, polygyny and concubinage, unilateral divorce and revocation, and a larger share of booty; Rāzī says these leave women vulnerable and make men more bound to fulfill their rights, since greater blessings make abuse more culpable.
rows.anchor: أن الرجل أزيد في الفضيلة من النساء في أمور أحدها : العقل والثاني : في الدية والثالث : في المواريث

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Rāzī cites the Prophet's instruction to treat women well, describing them as captives in men's care.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( استوصوا بالنساء خيرا فإنهن عندكم عوان )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī cites another report urging care for two vulnerable groups, the orphan and the woman.
rows.anchor: وفي خبر آخر : اتقوا الله في الضعيفين : اليتيم والمرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading sees marital benefits as shared: marriage brings tranquility, affection, love, kinship, helpers and friends, and pleasure; Rāzī even allows that the woman's share may be greater.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد حصول المنافع واللذة مشترك بين الجانبين ، لأن المقصود من الزوجية السكن والألفة والمودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, the husband bears additional duties of dowry, maintenance, defense, meeting her needs, and protecting her from harm; the wife's duty of service is therefore stronger in recognition of his added obligations, as 4:34 says.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الزوج اختص بأنواع من حقوق الزوجة ، وهي التزام المهر والنفقة ، والذب عنها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Rāzī cites the Prophet saying that, if he were to command prostration to anyone besides God, he would command a wife to prostrate to her husband.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لو أمرت أحدا بالسجود لغير الله لأمرت المرأة بالسجود لزوجها )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is invincible and cannot be prevented; His rulings and acts are sound and cannot involve purposelessness, folly, error, or falsehood.
rows.anchor: أي غالب لا يمنع ، مصيب أحكامه وأفعاله ، لا يتطرق إليهما احتمال العبث والسفه والغلط والباطل

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: In the divorce discussion, Abū Ḥanīfa holds that a prohibited divorce is sinful yet takes effect, based on the principle that prohibition does not entail invalidity.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : وهو قول أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه : أنه وإن كان محرما إلا أنه يقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers reading 2:229 as continuing 2:228: the earlier verse grants the husband revocation but leaves its limit unspecified, and this verse clarifies that revocable divorce occurs twice only, with no revocation after the second.
rows.anchor: أنها ليست كلاما مبتدأ ، بل هي متعلقة بما قبلها ، وذلك لأنه تعالى بين في الآية الأولى أن حق المراجعة ثابت للزوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-ṭalāq refers back to the previously discussed revocable divorce; linking the verses supplies an immediate specification or clarification, which Rāzī prefers to leaving the earlier ruling general or ambiguous and delaying its explanation.
rows.anchor: بالألف واللام في قوله : الطلاق للمعهود السابق ، يعني ذلك الطلاق الذي حكمنا فيه بثبوت الرجعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If 2:229 began an independent statement, its wording would wrongly restrict all divorce to twice, contrary to consensus; “release with kindness” cannot supply a third divorce, because it modifies retaining, does not itself imply divorce, and would make the next verse describe an impossible fourth divorce.
rows.anchor: كان قوله : { الطلاق مرتان } يقتضي حصر كل الطلاق في المرتين وهو باطل بالإجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī defines kind release as paying the woman's financial rights, not speaking ill of her after separation, and not discouraging people from marrying her.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن المراد من الإحسان ، هو أنه إذا تركها أدى إليها حقوقها المالية ، ولا يذكرها بعد المفارقة بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The right of return twice lets someone discover, after separation, whether parting is painful; two opportunities give experience of that feeling, allowing him to retain her decently if that is best or release her well, a gradual arrangement expressing God's mercy.
rows.anchor: المسألة الثالثة : الحكمة في إثبات حق الرجعة أن الإنسان ما دام يكون مع صاحبه لا يدري أنه هل تشق عليه مفارقته أو لا
